Key observations from the test image:
- Mixed healthy green plants with severely dead/dying stems in the center
- Dead stems appear bleached/whitish-tan
- Dead leaves remain attached to dead stems
- Pods visible (dried)
- Possible white cottony material on stems near soil level

Top candidates: White_Mold, Diaporthe, Phytophthora, Anthracnose. Let me check reference images.
The White_Mold top-right reference panel looks nearly identical to the test image — dead bleached stems surrounded by healthy green plants. Let me verify with a few more candidates.
Anthracnose shows dry late-season pods, SDS shows interveinal chlorosis, Phomopsis shows pod lesions — none match. Let me check a few more to be thorough.

Comparing all candidates:

- **Brown_Stem_Rot** (top-left): Shows dead patches in field, but with interveinal chlorosis and brown pith
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Darker gray stems with ashy specks
- **Fusarium**: Root/stem close-ups, not field canopy view

The test image most strongly matches **White_Mold**:
- The White_Mold reference top-right panel shows nearly identical canopy appearance: bleached dead stems surrounded by healthy green plants
- Dead leaves remaining attached to dead stems
- Bleached/whitened stem appearance
- "Patch" of death pattern in the canopy
- Some white fibrous material visible on stems
